validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: All five findings were checked against the working tree at HEAD (d51b0f0). Four reproduce exactly as written; the fifth reproduces with the nuance the reviewer gave. The largest change (recalculate.ts) was prototyped, typechecked and run against the full 421-test reports suite green, then reverted, so the plan's shape is known to compile and pass. validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #78 carries five non-blocking findings the review of PR #76 raised and approved despite. None is a behavioural bug: all five are about code that works but is fragile to read, easy to drift, or dead. I re-checked each against the working tree rather than taking the reviewer's word.

(1) recalculate.ts:99-102 — REPRODUCES. The Weekly branch's final bucket computes intervalEndDate from getEffectiveEndDate(endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx), so the label depends on the caller-supplied invariant that the last element of `intervals` is weekFromDate(endDate). Pre-#76 it computed getWeekEnd(intervalItem) from the bucket's own label and was correct for any intervals array. Both in-tree callers (custom-spreadsheet.ts:166-171, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:104-109) do build intervals via weekRangeInclusive(startDate, endDate, ...), whose last element is weekFromDate(end) (months.ts:292-311 pushes `week` once it equals endWeek), and getWeekEnd is constant within a week — so the equivalence holds today and the nine-line comment at :91-98 records the invariant without enforcing it.

(2) grouped-spreadsheet.ts:56-58 — REPRODUCES. The comment reads 'Same rule as custom-spreadsheet', but #76 deleted the five-line canonical comment at custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-125 and replaced it with a bare call; that file no longer contains the rule. The rule now lives only in the JSDoc at reportRanges.ts:89-103, which neither caller names.

(3) custom-spreadsheet.test.ts budgetMonths — REPRODUCES. Declared in runCustom's return type at :133, produced at :162, and read by nobody: all seven destructurings of runCustom's result (:218, :232, :245, :258, :268, :287, :444) omit it, and the four budget assertions at :380, :390, :398, :405 all call the module-level getBudgetMonths() accessor instead. Dead field on a helper with eleven other call sites.

(4) the seven-line budgeted-path rationale — REPRODUCES. I confirmed custom-spreadsheet.ts:144-150 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:82-88 are byte-identical (compared them programmatically). The work order behind #76 asked for byte-identical comments as a drift guard; the reviewer is right that identical prose in two files is a second copy to maintain, not a guard.

(5) ReportSummary.test.tsx getHeader — REPRODUCES with the reviewer's nuance. The helper's doc comment (:32-37) justifies itself by the yearly case, where the range collapses to a bare year and only exact textContent works. But getHeader is applied at :140 and :156 as well, and those two assert full header strings ('09/28/2026 to 10/04/2026', '09/28/2026 to 10/03/2026') that are structurally identical to the six the file asserts via screen.getByText — same <Text>, same two expression children (ReportSummary.tsx:92-96). I verified the reviewer's proposed fix rather than assuming it: I converted both to screen.getByText, ran the file, and all 9 tests passed, then restored the file. So getByText does work at both sites; the DOM walk is not needed there.

Nothing else in the tree reads these. recalculate has exactly two callers — custom-spreadsheet.ts:289 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:113 and :131 (the other functions named recalculate in this repo — crossover-spreadsheet.ts:214, calendar-spreadsheet.ts:140, cash-flow-spreadsheet.tsx:148, net-worth-spreadsheet.ts:364 — are unrelated private helpers in their own files, not this module). getEffectiveEndDate has four callers: the two factories, ReportSummary.tsx:54, and reportRanges' own test.
validated_work_order.root_cause: #76 consolidated the weekly end-date rule out of custom-spreadsheet into the shared getEffectiveEndDate helper, and the consolidation carried three artefacts that the helper's existence made redundant: a cross-reference naming a file that no longer held the rule, a duplicated block of prose that the helper's JSDoc now carries, and a caller that re-derives a value its own caller already computed. The comment/test findings are the same shape — a helper was introduced and the older scaffolding around it was left standing.
validated_work_order.approach:
One work order, five edits, each closing one finding with the smallest change that removes the problem rather than documenting it.

For finding 1 I take the reviewer's first option (pass the effective value from the caller) over the second (export a type or assertion tying a Weekly intervals array to its endDate). The type/assertion option encodes the invariant the reviewer is worried about — that intervals is derived from endDate — which is exactly the coupling to remove; a branded array type would make a future caller satisfy a constraint rather than stop depending on it. Passing the value is also smaller: recalculate already receives endDate, and both call sites already compute effectiveEndDate two lines earlier for their query bound (custom-spreadsheet.ts:121, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:59). So the prop swaps endDate+interval+firstDayOfWeekIdx for effectiveEndDate, and recalculate stops calling getEffectiveEndDate and stops importing it. Net: three props out, one in, one import gone, and the invariant disappears rather than being documented.

I prototyped this exact change, ran `yarn typecheck` (all 10 workspaces green) and `yarn workspace @actual-app/web vitest --run src/components/reports/` (26 files, 421 tests green), then reverted it. The implementer is writing the same change; the prototype exists to prove the shape compiles and that the 421 green tests are what this change is expected to preserve.

For finding 5 I take the reviewer's primary fix (use getByText at both sites, keep getHeader for the yearly case) over the alternative (keep the DOM walk and rename the helper), and I verified it passes before writing it down. The reviewer's secondary point stands and I am folding it in: the pair at :130-157 exists to prove the pref reaches the header, so the helper's doc comment must be narrowed to say it is for reading the header node itself — which after this change is only the yearly case.

For finding 4 I compress both copies to one sentence rather than deleting both. The reviewer offered three options; deleting both is tempting because the budgeted-path test at custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:392-425 already carries the premise as executable evidence, but that test proves the premise holds, not why the guard is budgeted-only — a reader at the guard is the one who needs the sentence. One sentence, identical in both files, is not the reviewer's complaint: the complaint is seven lines of reasoning the helper's JSDoc already carries. The premise itself (budget rows are month-keyed, weekly buckets are week-start-keyed) stays, compressed, because it is the part a reader cannot see in the two lines of code below the comment.

No new dependency, no new abstraction, no behaviour change anywhere. Every criterion that can be checked in a browser is one that checks the app still behaves as it did on HEAD.

qa_script: Boot the app (yarn start, port 3001), open the initial setup screen and choose 'View demo' — the empty budget will not exercise a weekly report with a final week in progress.
Reports -> Net Worth (or Spending). Set the interval dropdown to Weekly.

Set the To date to a week start strictly before today — e.g. if today is 2026-10-04 (a Sunday), pick 2026-09-27. Read the summary header range: it must end at today (2026-10-04's week already ended) or at the week's true end, never at the week start.
Compare the graph view against the table view (the report's table toggle): the final column must cover the same days in both. This is the pair the grouped-spreadsheet comment exists to protect.
Change the first day of week in Settings (Sunday -> Monday) and reload. The final weekly column must shift by exactly one day in the same direction, and the header must agree with it.
Switch the interval to Monthly and Daily: the header and final column must fall back to the raw end date exactly as they do on the base branch.
Open a report with the balance type 'Total Budgeted' at Weekly interval and confirm no error and no figure change against the base branch.
Compare every figure and every range above against the base branch. Any difference is a regression in a work order whose entire claim is that it changes no behaviour.
risks: The largest change is a signature change on an exported function. recalculate is called from exactly three places, all in this repo and all named in files[] — custom-spreadsheet.ts:289, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:113 and :131 — so the blast radius is closed, and TypeScript will catch a missed one at `yarn typecheck` rather than at runtime. I verified the grep for every `recalculate` in the tree: the similarly-named functions in crossover-spreadsheet.ts, calendar-spreadsheet.ts, cash-flow-spreadsheet.tsx and net-worth-spreadsheet.ts are unrelated private helpers.

The nested per-category recalculate call in grouped-spreadsheet.ts is indented four spaces deeper than the outer one and is formatted identically apart from that, which is exactly the shape of an edit an implementer applies to one and misses. Typecheck catches it (the old props would be unknown and effectiveEndDate required), and the three 'weekly grouped report end bound' cases would fail too.

AC-1 and AC-9 are browser checks that depend on the demo budget containing transactions spanning a week boundary in the current period. If the demo data does not reach the current week, QA should set the To date to the most recent week start the data does reach and compare against the base branch under the identical setting — the point of the check is equality with base, not a particular date.

No forbidden path is touched. Nothing under .sdlc/**, .github/**, docs/spec/**, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md is in files[]; upcoming-release-notes/ is not forbidden and has direct precedent in clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md.
No host outside env.api_allowlist is involved — this change makes no network call of any kind and adds no dependency.
out_of_scope: Making the intervals/endDate invariant type-safe (the reviewer's second option for finding 1 — exporting a branded Weekly intervals type or an assertion). This change removes the dependency instead of typing it, so the invariant no longer exists to enforce. If a future caller reintroduces a caller-supplied end date, that is a different ticket.
The eleven other runCustom call sites mentioned in finding 3's evidence. Only the dead return field is removed; the helper's signature otherwise stays as it is.

Renaming getHeader to say what it reads, which the reviewer offered as an alternative for finding 5. Narrowing the doc comment achieves the same result at a fraction of the diff; the helper has one caller left and the name is not misleading.

Any change to the budget-remap guard itself, to the widening above it, or to budgetDataQuery.ts's month keying. This work order documents and de-duplicates the guard's rationale; it does not alter when the guard applies.

Adding a test for a third caller of recalculate, or for a Weekly intervals array not derived from endDate. The change removes that dependency rather than defending against it, so such a test would assert a state the code can no longer reach.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: Single-agent plan (councils.plan is set to council in .sdlc/config.yml, but this run was a single planner). The one contested decision was finding 1's fix: the reviewer offered two — pass the effective value from the caller, or export a type/assertion tying a Weekly intervals array to its endDate. I took the first and rejected the second on the grounds that a branded type encodes the exact invariant the finding is about (that intervals derives from endDate), making a future caller satisfy the coupling rather than stop depending on it. To avoid planning an untested refactor on reasoning alone I applied the change to all three call sites, ran `yarn typecheck` (10/10 workspaces green) and the reports suite (421 tests green), then reverted. The second contested point was finding 4, where the reviewer offered compression or deletion; I compressed, because the budgeted-path test carries the month-keying premise as executable evidence but not the question a reader at the guard actually has. Finding 5's fix was verified empirically rather than argued: the conversion was applied, the file was run (9/9 pass), and the file was restored before the work order was written, so the plan does not ask the implementer to bet on an assertion form I had not exercised.
residual_risks: QA reads this first: four of the ten acceptance criteria are not browser-observable. Findings 2, 3, 4 and 5 are a stale cross-reference, a dead return field, a duplicated comment and a test-assertion style — none of them changes what a user sees, and no browser can confirm any of them. They are marked verify: test with the specific CI case or the specific grep in how_to_verify. AC-1 and AC-9 are the browser checks, and together they are the only thing that would catch a behaviour change.

A refactor work order with no behavioural acceptance is exactly the shape where a slipped edit goes unnoticed because the visible output is unchanged by design. AC-9 (step through every interval and both first-day-of-week settings, compare to base) and AC-10 (the three CI commands) are the net; if QA skips both, this work order has verified nothing.

The compressed budgeted-path comment is a judgement about how much prose a reader needs, and it is the change most likely to draw a review objection on merge. The full reasoning is recoverable from the reviewer's own evidence and from the test at custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:392-425, so nothing is lost irreversibly if a maintainer wants the longer form back.
